trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use travel time to rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport around 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€5.90) or Metro L9 Sud to the city center — both are budget-friendly options. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample and freshen up. Take a leisurely orientation walk along Passeig de Gràcia to spot the famous 'Block of Discord' featuring Gaudí's Casa Batlló (admire the exterior for free), Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera. Get your bearings in the Eixample grid layout.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the nearby Rambla de Catalunya for a relaxed evening atmosphere. Explore the lively Eixample bar scene — the area known as 'Gayxample' around Carrer del Consell de Cent has buzzing terraces perfect for a first night out. Enjoy a nightcap at a local bar and soak in the Barcelona vibe.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick bocadillo (sandwich) from a kiosk at the airport for around €3–5.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh baguette sandwich or slice of tortilla española from a local bakery or supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl nearby) for €3–6.
meals.dinner: Bar Calders (Carrer del Parlament) or a local menú del día restaurant in Eixample — a 3-course meal with wine for €12–15. Look for signs saying 'Menú' in the window.

day_by_day.notes: August in Barcelona is hot (30°C+). Pack light, stay hydrated, and carry a reusable water bottle — tap water is safe to drink. Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) upon arrival for big transport savings throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with Gaudí's masterpiece — La Sagrada Família. Book tickets online in advance to save time and potentially get discounted entry (€26 standard, €36 with tower access). Arrive at opening time (9:00) to beat the crowds and the worst of the heat. Spend 1.5–2 hours marveling at the interior light, the Nativity and Passion facades, and the surrounding park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to Park Güell (€10 entry for the Monumental Zone — book online). Explore Gaudí's mosaic terraces, the hypostyle room, and the Dragon Stairway. The surrounding free park areas offer panoramic views of the city — bring snacks and water. Afterward, descend through the Gràcia neighborhood, a bohemian district full of independent boutiques and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Eixample and explore the nightlife scene. Barcelona's nightlife starts late — dinner at 21:00 is normal. After dinner, head to one of the rooftop bars in Eixample for city views, or start bar-hopping around Carrer d'Enric Granados (a pedestrian boulevard lined with terrace bars). Clubs don't fill up until midnight–1:00 AM, so pace yourself.

meals.breakfast: Café and croissant or pan con tomate (bread with tomato) at a local café near the hotel for €3–5. Try Bar Calvet or any neighborhood café.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a nearby Lidl or Mercadona supermarket (baguette, cheese, fruit, drinks) and eat in Park Güell's free zone — budget €5–7 total.
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — tapas-style dishes, great value. Budget €15–20 per person including drinks. Arrive before 21:00 to avoid a long wait.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online at least a few days in advance — they sell out fast in August. Wear comfortable shoes as there's significant walking on uneven terrain at Park Güell.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) — take the metro to Jaume I. Explore the ancient Roman ruins, the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 and after 17:30 on weekdays), and the narrow medieval streets. Visit Plaça Reial and the Pont del Bisbe bridge. This entire area is free to wander and packed with architectural history spanning 2,000 years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to El Born neighborhood, adjacent to the Gothic Quarter. Visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar (free entry, stunning Gothic architecture) and the Born Cultural Centre (€6, houses ruins of 1714 Barcelona beneath a 19th-century iron market). Stroll along Passeig del Born for people-watching. If the heat is intense, duck into the free Museu Picasso courtyard or browse the cool interiors of the Born market.
day_by_day.evening: El Born is one of Barcelona's best nightlife neighborhoods. Start with vermouth (vermut) at a traditional bar around 19:00 — Bar del Pla or El Xampanyet are local favorites. As the night progresses, the area fills with locals and travelers alike. Bar-hop along Carrer del Rec and surrounding streets. This area is more relaxed than the club scene — perfect for architecture lovers who also enjoy a lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Pan con tomate and café amb llet at a Gothic Quarter café — €4–6. Try any bar displaying 'Esmorzar' (breakfast) signs.
meals.lunch: Mercat de Santa Caterina (less touristy alternative to La Boqueria) — grab fresh produce, olives, cheese, and snacks for a self-assembled lunch for €6–8. Eat at the market benches.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet (Carrer de Montcada) — a legendary local bar serving house cava and tapas. Budget €12–18 per person. Arrive early (19:30) as it gets packed quickly.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter is very crowded in August — be vigilant with your belongings, especially in tourist-heavy areas like La Rambla. Pickpocketing is common. Keep bags in front and avoid displaying expensive items.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Barceloneta beach for a morning swim before the crowds arrive (aim to be there by 9:00–9:30). The beach is free and the Mediterranean is warm in August. Walk along the Barceloneta promenade and admire Frank Gehry's iconic 'Fish' (Peix) sculpture — a stunning piece of contemporary architecture glinting in the morning sun. Explore the Barceloneta neighborhood's narrow 18th-century grid streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the bus up to Montjuïc hill. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (€14, worth it for the building and art) or opt for the free exterior viewing of the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe — a landmark of modernist architecture (entry €10, but the exterior is viewable for free). The Olympic Stadium exterior is also free to view. Take the cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc, €12.70 return) for panoramic views of the city and port.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and enjoy the magic hour light on the architecture of Eixample. Tonight, experience Barcelona's famous nightclub scene — Sala Apolo, Nitsa Club, or Razzmatazz are iconic venues with entry fees of €10–20 (often cheaper with guest list or early entry before midnight). Pre-party at a bar in Eixample or Poble Sec (near Montjuïc) where craft beer and cocktails are cheaper than in clubs.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh croissant and café from a beach-side kiosk or bakery in Barceloneta for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Supermarket picnic on the beach or a bocadillo from a local bar in Barceloneta for €4–7. Avoid the overpriced beach chiringuitos (beach bars) for full meals.
meals.dinner: Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec — Barcelona's 'pintxos street.' Load up on pintxos (small bites on bread) for €1–2 each. Budget €10–15 for a filling dinner with a drink. Perfect pre-club fuel.

day_by_day.notes: Montjuïc is accessible by metro to Paral·lel then cable car, or by Bus Turístic (not budget-friendly). The free Bus 150 from Plaça Espanya is the budget option up the hill. For clubs, check guest lists on Facebook or event apps like Xceed for free or discounted entry.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana in El Born — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most spectacular examples of Catalan Modernisme architecture. Guided tours cost €22 but the exterior alone is breathtaking and free to admire. Alternatively, if budget is tight, book the cheapest available concert ticket (sometimes from €15) for an authentic experience inside. Afterward, explore the surrounding Sant Pere neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your last afternoon at the Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC) on Montjuïc — entry is €12 (free on the first Sunday of the month and after 15:00 on Saturdays). The building itself is an architectural marvel from the 1929 International Exposition, and the collection spans Romanesque to modern Catalan art. The views from the front steps over the city and Plaça Espanya are iconic and completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Barcelona — return to Passeig de Gràcia for a farewell walk past the illuminated facades of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera). The buildings are dramatically lit after dark. Pick up any last souvenirs from local shops (avoid tourist traps on La Rambla — Eixample shops are better value). Enjoy a final dinner and cava toast to the trip.

meals.breakfast: Revisit your favorite neighborhood café or try a traditional granja (milk bar) for a chocolate con churros — €5–7. A classic Barcelona morning treat.
meals.lunch: Final menú del día at a local restaurant near MNAC or in Poble Sec — €12–15 for a full 3-course meal with wine. A great send-off lunch.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night — try Bodega Sepúlveda (Carrer de Sepúlveda, Eixample) for excellent Catalan cuisine at reasonable prices, €20–25 per person with wine. Or return to a favorite spot from earlier in the trip.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is early on August 20th, pack your bags tonight and confirm airport transport. The Aerobus runs from Plaça Catalunya from 05:00. Check out requirements with your accommodation. Leave a buffer of at least 2.5–3 hours before departure given August airport crowds. Total estimated trip budget (excluding flights and accommodation): €150–200 per person for 5 days, covering transport, entry fees, and meals.

trip_options.title: Classic Barcelona Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample via Aerobus (€6.75, ~35 min) or taxi (~€35). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided stroll along Passeig de Gràcia directly from the hotel to admire the 'Block of Discord' — Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera — from the outside. Pick up a cold drink at a terrace café and soak in the Eixample grid architecture at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Barcelona nightlife with dinner at a classic Eixample tapas bar, then a relaxed evening walk through the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia. Early night recommended to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or on arrival — nothing scheduled pre-landing.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana (Carrer de Mallorca, 236) — beloved local spot near the hotel for patatas bravas, croquetas, and fresh montaditos. Budget ~€15–20pp.
meals.dinner: Bar Calders (Carrer del Parlament, Sant Antoni area) — relaxed neighbourhood bar with excellent vermouth, pintxos, and small plates. Budget ~€20–25pp.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. August in Barcelona is very hot (30–35°C expected); stay hydrated. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance in case room isn't ready at 13:00 — many hotels offer luggage storage.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Book the skip-the-line guided tour (9:00 or 10:00 slot recommended). Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring Gaudí's iconic basilica inside and out, including the towers for panoramic views. The basilica is a 10-minute walk or short metro ride from Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience — Head to Las Ramblas for a deep dive into Barcelona's legendary covered market. Sample jamón ibérico, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and tapas from market stalls. Browse the stalls, interact with vendors, and enjoy a leisurely lunch inside the market.
day_by_day.evening: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour — Join a guided evening tour (many depart around 18:00–19:00) through Barcelona's medieval heart. Discover Roman ruins, Gothic cathedrals, and hidden plazas as the heat of the day subsides and the quarter glows in the golden evening light.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café (Carrer del Parlament, Eixample) — Australian-inspired brunch café, great coffee and avocado toast. Budget ~€10–14pp.
meals.lunch: Eat at La Boqueria Market itself — graze on fresh oysters, jamón, cheese, and fruit from various stalls. Budget ~€15–20pp for a satisfying market lunch.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet (Carrer de Montcada, El Born) — iconic cava bar near the Gothic Quarter serving house cava and traditional tapas in a historic setting. Budget ~€20–25pp.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets well in advance — August is peak season and slots sell out weeks ahead. Wear comfortable shoes for the Gothic Quarter evening walk on cobblestones. Keep valuables secure on Las Ramblas.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell Sunrise/Morning Visit — Arrive early (8:00–9:00) to beat the crowds and the afternoon heat. Explore Gaudí's whimsical mosaic-covered terraces, the hypostyle room, and the park's winding pathways. Enjoy panoramic views of the city from the main terrace. Take the metro to Lesseps and walk up, or take a taxi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gràcia neighbourhood at the foot of Park Güell — a charming, bohemian district with independent boutiques, colourful plazas (Plaça del Sol, Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia), and a very local feel. Browse architecture, street art, and relax at a shaded terrace bar during the hottest part of the day (14:00–17:00).
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach Club Nightlife Experience — Head down to Barceloneta for Barcelona's legendary beach nightlife. Start with sunset drinks at a chiringuito (beach bar) around 20:00, enjoy dinner al fresco, then move into the beach club scene as the night picks up after 23:00.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light breakfast near the hotel before heading out early — Forn de Sant Jaume (Rambla de Catalunya) for fresh pastries and café amb llet. Budget ~€5–8pp.
meals.lunch: La Pepita (Carrer de Montmany, Gràcia) — popular spot in Gràcia for creative montaditos and fresh salads. Budget ~€12–18pp.
meals.dinner: La Cova Fumada (Barceloneta) — legendary, no-frills local restaurant credited with inventing the bombas (meat croquettes). Cash only, arrive early. Budget ~€15–20pp. Follow with drinks at the beach clubs.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell's ticketed monumental zone requires timed entry — book online in advance. The beach nightlife scene starts late in Barcelona (clubs peak 01:00–05:00); pace yourself. Wear sunscreen for the morning park visit.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana — Visit this UNESCO World Heritage Site, a stunning Modernista concert hall by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Take a guided tour (45–60 min) of the breathtaking stained-glass interior. Afterwards, explore the El Born neighbourhood's boutique shops and galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc Hill Exploration — Take the Montjuïc cable car or funicular for sweeping city and sea views. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (mid-range entry ~€14), stroll the castle grounds, and enjoy the cooler hilltop breeze during the hottest afternoon hours. Explore the Olympic Stadium exterior from the 1992 Games.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop bar evening in Eixample — Return to the hotel district and enjoy Barcelona's rooftop bar scene. La Dolce Vitoria or the rooftop at Hotel Majestic offer stunning Eixample views. Then explore the Eixample Esquerra (left Eixample) 'Gayxample' area, known for its vibrant bars and nightlife energy.

meals.breakfast: Alsur Café (El Born area) — relaxed café with excellent brunch options near Palau de la Música. Budget ~€10–15pp.
meals.lunch: Bar del Pla (El Born) — beloved local bar with excellent croquetas, fresh fish, and Catalan classics. Budget ~€15–20pp.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda (Carrer de Sepúlveda, Eixample) — cosy wine bar and restaurant with great natural wines and seasonal Catalan dishes. Budget ~€25–35pp.

day_by_day.notes: Book Palau de la Música tour online to guarantee entry. Montjuïc is best in the afternoon when the light is golden — bring water. The Eixample rooftop bar scene is more relaxed than the beach clubs, ideal for a slightly quieter night mid-trip.

day_by_day.morning: Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) Interior Visit — Choose one of Gaudí's residential masterpieces on Passeig de Gràcia for a deep architectural experience. Casa Milà's rooftop warrior chimneys are iconic; Casa Batlló's interior is otherworldly. Both are steps from the hotel. Book timed entry in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxed afternoon in Eixample and Rambla de Catalunya — Browse the tree-lined Rambla de Catalunya (calmer alternative to Las Ramblas) for last-minute shopping, souvenirs, and people-watching at a terrace café. Pack bags and prepare for departure if flying out soon, or continue exploring at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Eixample — Splurge slightly on a memorable final meal at a quality Catalan restaurant. Then a last evening stroll along the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia to say goodbye to Barcelona's architectural grandeur.

meals.breakfast: Parking Pizza (Carrer de Londres, Eixample) — surprisingly great brunch spot with fresh juices, eggs, and pastries in a cool setting. Budget ~€10–14pp.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana (revisit or try Bodega Sepúlveda for a lighter lunch) — familiar favourite for a relaxed final lunch. Budget ~€15–20pp.
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza (dinner menu) or Moments Restaurant (splurge option, Mandarin Oriental) for a special farewell Catalan tasting menu. Mid-range farewell: Moments lite menu ~€45–60pp; casual option ~€25–30pp.

day_by_day.notes: Check out logistics: confirm hotel late checkout or luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. August flights from Barcelona El Prat can be busy — allow 2.5–3 hours before departure. Keep one Gaudí site for the final morning as a perfect architectural send-off.

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transfer from Barcelona El Prat Airport to the Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample via private luxury transfer (pre-booked black car service). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into the suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely stroll along Passeig de Gràcia, Eixample's grand boulevard, to admire the Block of Discord — Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera. Enjoy the architectural splendor at your own pace before the evening begins. Consider a private exterior guided commentary walk for context.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Disfrutar (2 Michelin stars), one of Barcelona's most celebrated avant-garde restaurants, offering a theatrical tasting menu that blends molecular gastronomy with Catalan tradition. Book the full tasting menu with wine pairing. After dinner, enjoy a nightcap at the rooftop bar of the Hotel Mandarin Oriental on Passeig de Gràcia for sweeping city views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or a light snack at the airport upon arrival — no formal breakfast scheduled.
meals.lunch: Upon settling in, visit Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca (5-minute walk from Eixample hotels) for premium tapas: patatas bravas, jamón ibérico, and fresh seafood montaditos paired with a crisp Catalan white wine.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar — avant-garde tasting menu with wine pairing. Budget approximately €250–€350 per person. Reservations essential and should be booked months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm Disfrutar reservation well ahead of travel. Passeig de Gràcia is walkable from most Eixample accommodations. August evenings are warm (~25°C), so light linen attire is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Skip-the-Line Guided Tour (9:00 AM). Enjoy an exclusive private guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica, including tower access for panoramic views. The morning light through the stained-glass windows on the Nativity façade side is spectacular — a must-see for architecture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell Sunset Visit — arrive in the late afternoon (around 17:00–18:00) to explore Gaudí's whimsical mosaic-covered park. Secure timed-entry tickets for the Monumental Zone. As the sun descends, the terrace offers breathtaking golden-hour panoramic views over Barcelona and the Mediterranean. A private guide can enrich the symbolism and design philosophy behind the park.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach Club Nightlife Experience. Head to the beachfront for Barcelona's legendary chiringuito scene. Begin with sundowners at Opium Beach or Pacha Barcelona, then transition to a premium beach club for dinner and dancing. VIP table reservations at Shôko or CDLC (Carpe Diem Lounge Club) offer bottle service, gourmet dining, and world-class DJs against a Mediterranean backdrop.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or visit Federal Café in Eixample for a gourmet brunch spread — avocado toast, smoked salmon, artisan coffees.
meals.lunch: Post-Sagrada Família, dine at Alkimia in the Eixample district — a Michelin-starred restaurant by chef Jordi Vilà offering refined modern Catalan cuisine. Opt for the tasting menu at lunch for a more accessible price point (~€90–€130 per person).
meals.dinner: CDLC (Carpe Diem Lounge Club) on Barceloneta beachfront — fusion Asian-Mediterranean cuisine with a vibrant nightlife atmosphere. Expect a premium à la carte menu; budget €80–€120 per person for dinner before the club experience begins.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tower access tickets online in advance — they sell out weeks ahead. Park Güell timed-entry tickets must also be pre-purchased. Wear comfortable walking shoes for both morning and afternoon. For the beach club evening, smart-casual to stylish attire is expected; some venues enforce a dress code.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour (10:00 AM). Embark on a private guided tour through Barcelona's medieval heart — explore Roman ruins beneath the city, the Gothic Cathedral (La Catedral de la Santa Creu i Santa Eulàlia), the ancient Jewish Quarter (El Call), hidden plazas like Plaça de Sant Felip Neri, and the Pont del Bisbe bridge. A private guide brings centuries of history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience. After the Gothic Quarter, walk to La Boqueria on La Rambla for a curated premium food experience. Join a guided tasting tour to sample jamón ibérico de bellota, artisan cheeses, fresh seafood, exotic fruits, and local vermouth. Follow with free time to browse the market's finest stalls and pick up gourmet souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's architectural nightlife fusion — visit Palau de la Música Catalana for an evening concert (check the August program for live performances in this UNESCO World Heritage modernist masterpiece by Domènech i Montaner). After the concert, explore El Born's cocktail bar scene: try Paradiso (ranked among the world's best bars) for a theatrical, speakeasy-style craft cocktail experience.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast at the hotel or visit Faborit on Passeig de Gràcia for premium pastries, fresh-squeezed juices, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Post-market, lunch at Bar del Pla in El Born — a beloved Catalan bistro offering elevated traditional dishes like bacallà a la llauna, croquetes de pernil, and fresh fish. Pair with a glass of local Priorat or Penedès wine.
meals.dinner: Tickets Bar by Albert Adrià (tapas avant-garde) — book the full experience for a playful, circus-themed tasting journey through innovative Spanish tapas. One of Barcelona's most coveted reservations; budget ~€120–€180 per person. Alternatively, Bodega 1900 (same group) offers a more relaxed vermouth-and-tapas format.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is busiest mid-morning; arrive with the guided group to navigate efficiently. Palau de la Música Catalana concert tickets should be purchased in advance via their official website. Paradiso cocktail bar has a queue system — arrive early or check for reservation options. Gothic Quarter cobblestones require comfortable footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Private Architecture Deep-Dive: Palau Güell & Eixample Modernisme. Begin with a private guided visit to Palau Güell (Gaudí's early masterpiece near the Ramblas), then return to Eixample for an in-depth interior tour of Casa Batlló — including the exclusive 'Magic Nights' evening experience or the morning immersive tour with augmented reality. This is essential for architecture enthusiasts seeking to understand Gaudí's evolution.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc & Pavilion Mies van der Rohe. Take a private car or cable car to Montjuïc hill. Visit the Barcelona Pavilion — Ludwig Mies van der Rohe's 1929 masterpiece of modernist architecture, a pilgrimage site for design lovers. Continue to the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class contemporary art in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert. Enjoy the terrace views over the city.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop and Skyline Nightlife Experience. Begin with cocktails at the rooftop terrace of El Nacional (a grand food hall and bar on Passeig de Gràcia) or the Ohla Barcelona rooftop. Then head to Eixample's 'Gayxample' district for the city's sophisticated cocktail and bar scene. End the night at Sala Apolo or Razzmatazz for world-renowned DJ sets and live music in architecturally interesting converted industrial venues.

meals.breakfast: Room service or hotel breakfast — take time to enjoy the morning before a full day. Alternatively, visit Baluard Barceloneta bakery (if passing through) for exceptional artisan bread and pastries.
meals.lunch: Quimet & Quimet in Poble Sec (near Montjuïc) — a legendary standing-bar bodega serving exceptional conservas (tinned seafood) and creative montaditos with premium vermouth. A beloved local institution despite its humble size.
meals.dinner: Lasarte (3 Michelin stars) by Martín Berasategui — Barcelona's pinnacle of fine dining, located in the Monument Hotel in Eixample. The tasting menu showcases extraordinary Basque-Catalan haute cuisine. Budget €300–€400 per person with wine pairing. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló tickets are premium (~€35–€50) but worth every euro for the immersive experience. Book in advance. The Barcelona Pavilion is often uncrowded and deeply rewarding for architecture lovers. Montjuïc cable car offers scenic views; alternatively, a private car is more comfortable in August heat. Razzmatazz and Apolo typically open late (01:00 AM+); pace the evening accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau — Visit the extraordinary Hospital de Sant Pau, a UNESCO World Heritage modernist complex by Lluís Domènech i Montaner, just a short walk from Sagrada Família. Often overlooked by tourists, this is one of the most breathtaking architectural ensembles in Barcelona. Take a private guided tour to fully appreciate the Art Nouveau details, mosaics, and garden pavilions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon in El Born & Waterfront. Browse the high-end concept stores and galleries of El Born district. Visit the Museu Picasso (if desired) or simply enjoy the neighborhood's architectural heritage. Head to Port Olímpic for a final Mediterranean afternoon — consider a private yacht charter for 2–3 hours along the Barcelona coastline, taking in the city's skyline from the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Final Night Experience. Celebrate the journey's end with dinner at Moments (2 Michelin stars) in the Mandarin Oriental Hotel — chef Carme Ruscalleda's refined Catalan cuisine in an elegant setting. After dinner, enjoy a final stroll along the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia to admire the lit façades of Gaudí's masterpieces by night — a magical architectural farewell to Barcelona.

meals.breakfast: Grand hotel breakfast or visit Espai Mescladís in El Born for a social-enterprise brunch with excellent local produce and organic options.
meals.lunch: El Xampanyet in El Born — a classic cava bar and tapas spot beloved by locals and discerning visitors alike. Order the house cava, anchovies, and rotating tapas for a quintessential Barcelona lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Moments at Mandarin Oriental Barcelona — refined Catalan tasting menu with exceptional wine pairings. Budget €200–€300 per person. Smart-casual to formal attire required. End with digestifs at the Mandarin's elegant Banker's Bar.

day_by_day.notes: Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau is a 10-minute walk from Sagrada Família — consider combining the areas on this final morning. Private yacht charters should be booked 24–48 hours in advance; half-day options are available from Port Olímpic and Port Vell. Pack and arrange checkout/late checkout with the hotel in advance. Private transfer back to El Prat Airport should be pre-booked for departure day.
